cells.tense: You are here with the pen, and what is finishing is finishing cleanly.
cells.act: stand firm in the material hardship
cells.ask: When something you carried for a hope ends this week, stand still with it a minute before you replace it. Let the session, the budget, the plan be what it is. Then carry on.
cells.core:
What you've been building is completing, and you're not fighting the completion. You can carry a load a long stretch without losing your footing, and you decide what's finished and what continues. That decision is what makes a clearing survivable rather than a loss.

Before you refill a gap a finished thing left, don't refill it yet. Let the shelf stay empty, the file stay closed, the slot in the week stay quiet. Stay near it for a minute on your own reserves — not forever, just long enough to see what is still yours to keep. That pause is the part of this you are better at than you credit.
cells.sheetLine: What is ending is ending on your watch, and you're still here.
cells.verb: keep going on what was begun, after the beginning is gone
cells.place: the room where what is finished has been cleared to make space

cells.tense: You will be braced against an ending before it has arrived.
cells.act: hold two true things without declaring either
cells.ask: Take one ending you're braced for. Set its cost and its openness onto one page, side by side, and leave the page open — no verdict, no settling it. Return to it when the ending actually lands.
cells.core:
You are already at the far end of an ending that has not happened yet — planning the next chapter before the present one has finished closing. Some of what you call foresight is you not letting the end be the end. Underneath it, your instinct to keep going is real, tested many times, and accurate when you give it room. The strain is in trying to know how this closes before you know.

There is a page you can use instead of deciding in your head. Put the cost the ending will bring down, and the room it will open beside it, and hold both without picking one as the truth. Leave the page open. You do not have to declare anything now, and you can go back to it when the ending arrives.

cells.tense: You are still at a door that closed behind you.
cells.act: tend the resource with responsible care
cells.ask: For a week, give a steady hand to something live — a plant, a skill, a small need of someone near you — on schedule, asking nothing back and holding nothing tight. Keep it going past the week if it holds.
cells.core:
The ending already happened. You are past it and not through it, and the part of you that carried everything on hope is not carrying much now. That is not failure of strength — it is strength running on empty, and pushing it will not fill it. Trying harder at hope is not the move. Caring for something small enough that no effort is required is, because the care does the pulling.

Give a steady hand to one live thing in your week — water what will grow, keep a small commitment, look after one resource you still have instead of the one you lost. Ask nothing back from it, and don't hold so tight it costs you. Care you can afford, given on schedule, is how the line recharges. The bigger hope comes back to a hand that stayed open.

cells.tense: Your hand is still on the page while you say the page was never yours.
cells.act: carry your own share, all of it
cells.ask: At the next telling — to yourself counts — name one thing you did across a hard stretch, plainly, without timing or luck in the sentence.
cells.core:
You cleared what was finished and went on. When you tell it, the story lands as things ending on their own, timing working out, being lucky — and none of it says the thing that kept you upright: you persisted. That persistence is why the clearing worked, and it is still yours. You just haven't been signing it.

You don't have to declare it to anyone. Take the next time a hard stretch in your life comes up in your own telling, to yourself or to someone else, and give one plain sentence to what you did. No timing, no luck. The sentence after that is yours too. Persisting is one of the things that makes you who you are, and the account should have your handwriting in it.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim in my draft is that all four statuses read the same card-seat as a single story: the record supports Resilience at Fruition landing in Transformation, and Steadfastness/Reflection/Stewardship as the medicine signatures, but it does not support me telling the person what they are feeling about endings, who or what ended, or how long they have been carrying it. A reader could reasonably say the Too Much cell presumes they are over-managing a clear-out, and the Too Little cell presumes they are stuck at a door they already walked through — both are offered, not asserted. The asks survive being wrong: each one names a small act the person can do regardless of whether my read of the moment is right, and none makes progress conditional on the reading. The sentence that serves me more than them is the symmetrical Too Much/Too Little hinge describing one capacity failing in two directions — that is the derivation talking to me, not the reader, and I have kept it out of the cores and written the too-much and too-little cells as opposite failures of persistence itself.
